citation: Shivani Shukla, Himanshu Joshi, Romilla Syed. 'Security Degradation in Iterative AI Code Generation: A Systematic Analysis of the Paradox'. arXiv:2506.11022 (v2, 26 Sep 2025); accepted at IEEE ISTAS 2025. https://arxiv.org/abs/2506.11022
source_tier: Preprint, stated as peer-reviewed and accepted at IEEE ISTAS 2025 (conference)
access_status: HTML full text (v2) read via a fetch tool that summarises the page; the abstract was not reproduced verbatim and tables were read through that summary. Quotes below should be re-checked against the PDF [uncertain]
sponsor_and_incentive: No funding statement found. Academic authors (University of San Francisco; Vector Institute; UMass Boston). No product sold.
exact_quotes: Abstract: "Our findings show a 37.6% increase in critical vulnerabilities after just five iterations"
Section IV-C: "Human review between iterations is essential to detect these subtle security degradations"
Section VI: "We focused on OpenAI's GPT-4o."
Section VI: "Developers rarely use LLMs in fully autonomous iteration chains."
Section II-B (quoting Chong et al.): "upon prompting, LLM can introduce issues in files that were issues-free before prompting"
date_and_recency: arXiv first submitted May/June 2025 (ID 2506.11022); v2 dated 26 Sep 2025. Data collection window not stated [uncertain]
key_claims: Repeated LLM 'improvement' of code, with no human in the loop, increases vulnerabilities rather than reducing them (feedback loop security degradation). Even security-focused prompts did not eliminate new vulnerabilities. Vulnerability count correlates with code complexity growth. Authors recommend human review between iterations.
headline_figures: 37.6% increase in critical vulnerabilities after five iterations (abstract; per-iteration breakdown behind this number not located in body)
Table II total/critical vulnerabilities by strategy: efficiency-focused 124/37; feature-focused 158/29; security-focused 38/7; ambiguous 67/14 (total 387, critical 87)
Complexity correlation r = 0.64; 10% complexity increase associated with 14.3% increase in vulnerability count
sample_unit_and_population: 400 code samples: 10 baseline programs x 4 prompting strategies x 10 iterations (40 rounds). Languages C and Java. Model: OpenAI GPT-4o, temperature 0.7, top_p 1.0 (Section III-C); exact model snapshot/version string not captured [uncertain]. Detection: Clang Static Analyzer, CodeQL, SpotBugs plus manual security review, severity via CVSS. Small, synthetic, controlled; not real-world repos.
observed_vs_stated: Observed: controlled experiment with tool-detected and manually reviewed vulnerabilities, not self-report.
what_makes_trust_justified: Human review between LLM iterations; cap consecutive LLM-only iterations at three and reset after each human review; security review after every iteration; conventional static analysis between iterations; extra scrutiny when complexity rises (Section V-B).
what_it_costs: Human review checkpoints every few iterations and per-iteration security scanning; paper gives no quantified cost.
failure_mode_class: Security (vulnerabilities introduced or accumulated through repeated autonomous modification)
control_that_would_have_prevented: Not an incident study. Missing control in the experiment's loop: human review and static analysis gating between iterations.
limitations_stated: Only GPT-4o tested. Only C and Java. Pure LLM loops simulated without humans, which real development rarely does ("Developers rarely use LLMs in fully autonomous iteration chains.").
counter_evidence: Security-focused prompts produced far fewer vulnerabilities (38 total, 7 critical) than other strategies, so degradation depends on prompt. Internal oddities noted on reading: 37.6% appears only in abstract; per-iteration averages do not obviously reconcile with 387 total over 400 samples; text calls efficiency prompts most severe though feature-focused has the highest total. Small sample (10 baselines). A later paper (arXiv:2603.08520) reports similar degradation across three LLMs but was not opened [uncertain].
verification_status: Claims checked against the arXiv v2 HTML via a summarising fetch tool, not the raw PDF. Figures and quotes: partially verified; re-open the PDF before quoting. Table II figures [uncertain]. 37.6% figure verified only as an abstract claim.
usable_claim: In one controlled experiment with GPT-4o on 10 C and Java programs, repeatedly asking the model to improve its own code, with no human review, increased vulnerabilities as iterations rose, and the authors recommend human review between iterations.
do_not_use: Do not generalise to all models, languages or real-world agent use. Do not present 37.6% as a general rate or lean on the per-iteration averages. Do not say security prompts make code worse.
overlap_with_existing_essays: Not checked against the Verification Gap or Checking Isn't Catching essays [uncertain]
